summary:
**SKYVERSE — Explore the Changing Universe**

SKYVERSE is an interactive astronomical exploration and citizen-science platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx observations accessible, understandable and useful for discovering changes in the universe.

Addressing the challenge of analysing over a billion astronomical sources across 102 near-infrared spectral bands, SKYVERSE transforms complex astronomical data into an intuitive scientific workspace. Users can explore sky regions using Right Ascension and Declination, visualize available SPHEREx observations, and investigate changes through our flagship **Cosmic Time Machine**, featuring blink comparison, time-lapse, image overlay, difference imaging and positional inspection.

Our platform also introduces Spectral Intelligence for wavelength-based exploration, dedicated investigation workspaces for all five challenge targets, and a Citizen Discovery Hub where users can document and submit potential astronomical discoveries with supporting evidence.

By combining scientific visualization, multi-epoch investigation and public participation, SKYVERSE aims to bridge the gap between professional astronomical research and citizen science, empowering students, astronomy enthusiasts and researchers to participate in exploring the changing universe.
details:
SKYVERSE — Explore the Changing Universe

SKYVERSE is an interactive astronomical exploration and citizen-science platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx observations more accessible, understandable and easier to investigate.

The platform enables users to explore astronomical regions using Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, retrieve available SPHEREx observations and examine scientific image data and metadata. Its flagship feature, Cosmic Time Machine, offers five visualization modes: Blink Comparator, Time-Lapse, Image Overlay, Difference View and Position Inspection, helping users investigate possible positional shifts and brightness variations across observation epochs.

SKYVERSE also features Spectral Intelligence, which enables exploration of SPHEREx's 102 near-infrared spectral channels, and dedicated investigation workspaces for five challenge targets: Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae and R Draconis. Gaia DR3 is incorporated as a complementary astrometric reference wherever reliable cross-matching is available. The Citizen Discovery Hub provides a structured environment for documenting observations, submitting supporting evidence and tracking potential discoveries.

The project aims to bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and public participation in scientific exploration. Its intended impact is to empower students, educators, amateur astronomers and citizen scientists to engage with real astronomical data and contribute to evidence-based investigations.

The technology stack includes React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion for the frontend, with Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy and Astroquery supporting scientific data processing and backend workflows. PostgreSQL can support investigation records and user-submitted reports.

What makes SKYVERSE creative is its integration of time-domain visualization, spectral exploration and citizen-science participation into a unified, user-friendly experience. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, image alignment, observation quality, uncertainty, accessibility, usability, scalability and the clear separation of SPHEREx and NEOSSat datasets.

Our vision is to make astronomical discovery more accessible, collaborative and driven by curiosity — empowering more people to explore and understand the changing universe.
